learn.title: Two equal ratios
learn.body: A proportion says two ratios are equal, such as $\frac{3}{4}=\frac{9}{12}$. Proportions appear whenever things scale together: recipes, speed, prices. If you know three of the four numbers, you can find the fourth.

learn.title: The multiplier
learn.body: Look at how one ratio becomes the other. In $\frac{3}{4}=\frac{x}{12}$ the bottom goes from 4 to 12, which is times 3. So the top must also be times 3: $x=3\times 3=9$.

learn.title: Scale a recipe
learn.body: 2 cups of rice make 6 servings. How many cups make 15 servings?

learn.title: Checking with cross products
learn.body: In a true proportion the cross products are equal. For $\frac{2}{6}=\frac{5}{15}$ we get $2\times 15=30$ and $6\times 5=30$. If the two products differ, the ratios are not equal.
Keep the same quantity on top on both sides. Cups over servings on the left means cups over servings on the right.

questions.explanation: Cross products: $3\times 12=36$ and $4\times 9=36$. The others do not match.
